question: Should OpenClaw accept a generic durable plugin allow-always API now, and what stable non-sensitive owner/scope should the built-in Skill Workshop path use if it opts in?
rationale: This changes a plugin API and a persistent approval security boundary, and automation cannot choose whether durable approval reuse belongs in core, plugin-specific policy, or a narrower Skill Workshop follow-up.

options.title: Fix durable scope before merge
options.body: Require the branch to add a stable owner id, replace request-visible workspace paths with a non-sensitive scope, preserve current-main approval fields, and prove second-call reuse.

options.title: Accept the API as-is intentionally
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept the compatibility and security-boundary tradeoff, but should document upgrade and request-visible key expectations before merge.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop opt-in out
options.body: Land only the generic backend after API review and keep Skill Workshop on allow-once/deny until its audit and owner model is settled.

recommendation.title: Fix durable scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require the branch to add a stable owner id, replace request-visible workspace paths with a non-sensitive scope, preserve current-main approval fields, and prove second-call reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is centered on the plugin approval framework contract that joshavant introduced and has adjacent ownership for.
